name: Format

hero.title: Change the language once. Every price and date follows.
hero.lede: `formatCurrency(price, 'EUR')` is one function over the platform's `Intl`. Read it in JSX and its text updates when the locale does, with no component re-rendering. The same call runs in plain code and on the server, and a `/core` entry with no dependencies carries it everywhere else.

why.title: Every number in your app, in the reader's language.

items.title: One call switches everything
items.text: `setLocale('de')` and every formatted price, date and size on screen rewrites its own text node. Components do not re-render, and inputs keep their caret.

items.title: One function per job
items.text: `formatCurrency`, `formatBytes`, `formatDuration`, `formatList`, `formatRelativeTo`. Plain data in, a string out: no classes, and no formatter object to build or pass around.

items.title: Dates that stay put
items.text: A date string with no time is a calendar date: the same day in every zone, so `'2026-11-18'` never becomes the 17th for someone in Los Angeles. An instant (`Z`, an offset, a number, a `Date`) is shown in the zone you pick.

items.title: Parsing is the other half
items.text: `parseNumber('1 234,5', { locale: 'cs' })` is 1234.5 and `parseDate('18. 11. 2026', { locale: 'cs' })` is `'2026-11-18'`. What the visitor typed in their own format becomes a number or a date, and anything else is `null`.

difference.title: The locale stops being an argument.

before.label: Intl by hand
before.caption: The locale is a parameter of every call, a formatter is built each time, and a plain date string needs a UTC workaround.

after.label: with @pyreon/format
after.caption: The active locale is a signal. Each call reads it, so the text updates when it changes.

comingFrom.title: The same strings, without building the formatter.
comingFrom.after:
import { formatCurrency, formatDate, setLocale } from '@pyreon/format'

setLocale('de')
formatCurrency(1234.5, 'EUR')      // "1.234,50 €"
formatDate('2026-11-18', 'long')   // "18. November 2026"
comingFrom.note: Checked against raw `Intl` for these two calls: the output is the same string, because `Intl` does the formatting. What changes is who builds and caches the formatter, and where the locale comes from. A calendar string needs no `timeZone: 'UTC'` workaround.

comingFrom.title: Sizes and durations in the reader's language.
comingFrom.before:
import prettyBytes from 'pretty-bytes'
import prettyMs from 'pretty-ms'

prettyBytes(1536)                              // "1.54 kB"
prettyBytes(1536, { locale: 'de' })            // "1,54 kB"
prettyMs(3_905_000)                            // "1h 5m 5s"
prettyMs(3_905_000, { colonNotation: true })   // "1:05:05"
comingFrom.after:
import { formatBytes, formatDuration } from '@pyreon/format'

formatBytes(1536)                                // "1.5 kB"
formatBytes(1536, { locale: 'de' })              // "1,5 kB"
formatDuration(3_905_000)                        // "1 hr, 5 min, 5 sec"
formatDuration(3_905_000, { style: 'digital' })  // "1:05:05"
comingFrom.note: pretty-bytes keeps three significant digits (`1.54 kB`); `formatBytes` shows one fraction digit (`1.5 kB`), and `maximumFractionDigits` changes it. pretty-ms prints English unit letters; `formatDuration` follows the locale's unit names. Both libraries are smaller for one job: pretty-ms is 1.2 kB gzip and `formatDuration` is 2.0 kB.

comingFrom.title: One active locale instead of an instance per locale.
comingFrom.before:
import { createIntl } from '@formatjs/intl'

const intl = createIntl({ locale: 'de' })
intl.formatNumber(1234.5, { style: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' })   // "1.234,50 €"
intl.formatRelativeTime(-3, 'day')                                  // "vor 3 Tagen"
comingFrom.after:
import { formatCurrency, formatRelative, setLocale } from '@pyreon/format'

setLocale('de')
formatCurrency(1234.5, 'EUR')   // "1.234,50 €"
formatRelative(-3, 'day')       // "vor 3 Tagen"
comingFrom.note: `@formatjs/intl` also formats ICU messages (plurals, selects); this package does not. Messages stay in `@pyreon/i18n`. For numbers, dates and relative time the output is the same strings, at 1.1 kB for a number against 13.1 kB gzip.

demo.title: Switch the language. Switch the zone. Everything moves.
demo.text: One locale and one time zone drive every value below, through the real `@pyreon/format`. Type a number the way you would in that language and `parseNumber` reads it back. The calendar date stays on the 18th when the zone changes; the instant does not.
demo.reference: built against the real package in the site repository; no canvas prototype

items.name: Numbers, currency, percent
items.text: `formatNumber`, `formatCurrency` and `formatPercent` take the options `Intl` has, plus presets for the common shapes.

items.name: Compact and units
items.text: `formatCompact(1_240_000)` is `1.2M`; `formatUnit(72, 'kilometer-per-hour')` is `72 km/h`. A unit `Intl` does not have is a type error.

items.name: Bytes, decimal or binary
items.text: `1.5 kB` or, with `binary: true`, `1.5 KiB`. Rounding never prints `1000 kB`: the value carries into the next unit.

items.name: Durations
items.text: Milliseconds or `{ hours, minutes }`; `largest: 2` keeps the two biggest units, `style: 'digital'` gives `1:05:05`. Uses `Intl.DurationFormat` where it exists and an equivalent where it does not.

items.name: Lists
items.text: `formatList(['red', 'green', 'blue'])` joins the way the language does: `and`, `or`, or a plain unit list.

items.name: Dates and times
items.text: `formatDate`, `formatTime`, `formatDateTime` with `short` to `full` presets, or any `Intl.DateTimeFormat` options.

items.name: Relative time and ranges
items.text: `formatRelativeTo(target, base)` picks the unit (`yesterday`, `in 5 minutes`); `formatDateRange` and `formatNumberRange` collapse the shared parts.

items.name: Named formats
items.text: `defineFormats({ price: { kind: 'currency', currency: 'EUR' } })` names a set once. Keys, value types and overrides are inferred; a wrong `kind` or `unit` is a type error.

items.name: `<Num>` and `<DateTime>`
items.text: `<Num>` renders reactive text with no wrapper element. `<DateTime>` renders a real `<time datetime>` whose machine-readable value does not depend on the display locale.

items.name: Bounded caches, safe on data
items.text: Each `Intl` formatter is built once per locale and options, in tables with a size cap. Nullish input returns the `fallback` and bad data never throws; a wrong option throws a `[Pyreon]` error that says how to fix it.

recipes.title: A price list that follows the language
recipes.text: Name the formats once at module level. Each cell reads the active locale, so one `setLocale` rewrites the whole table.

recipes.title: A time zone switcher that never moves a birthday
recipes.text: A calendar date stays on its day in every zone. An instant is shown in the zone you set. `new Date('2026-11-18')` is an instant at midnight UTC, so pass the string.
recipes.code:
import { formatDate, formatDateTime, setTimeZone } from '@pyreon/format'

const birthday = '2026-11-18'            // a calendar date
const standup = '2026-11-18T23:30:00Z'   // an instant

setTimeZone('Asia/Tokyo')
formatDate(birthday)                     // "Nov 18, 2026"
formatDateTime(standup)                  // "Nov 19, 2026, 8:30 AM"

setTimeZone('America/Los_Angeles')
formatDate(birthday)                     // "Nov 18, 2026"
formatDateTime(standup)                  // "Nov 18, 2026, 3:30 PM"
formatDate(new Date(birthday))           // "Nov 17, 2026"  ← the instant, not the date

recipes.title: Read what the visitor typed
recipes.text: Parse with the locale the visitor types in. `1.234` is 1234 in German and 1.234 in English, so the locale is part of the question.

limits.title: Experimental
limits.text: The API may change in a minor release before it is promoted to Stable. Pin the version while you build on it, and read the changelog when you update.

limits.title: A provided locale is visible in setup and effects
limits.text: `provideLocale` is context. A formatter called in a component body, an effect, a computed or a JSX accessor sees it. One called from an event handler outside any scope sees the app default, so format in setup and keep the string if a handler needs it.

limits.title: On the server, provide the locale per request
limits.text: One process serves many requests, so `setLocale` does nothing there (and warns in development). Call `provideLocale` and `provideTimeZone` in the root component; they are request-scoped and never share a locale between requests.

limits.title: Parsing covers numbers and numeric dates
limits.text: `parseDate` reads numeric dates in the locale's order and ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`. Month names (`18 November 2026`), other calendars and scientific notation return `null`.

limits.title: Engines differ in CLDR data
limits.text: `Intl` output is CLDR data, and V8, JavaScriptCore and ICU versions differ (a narrow no-break space before PM, for one). Pass the same locale and time zone on the server and in the browser; byte equality across engines is not promised.

limits.title: iOS and Android are not covered yet
limits.text: The package is web-only today. A core set of `Intl` number and date calls already lowers to the native targets without it; mapping these functions onto that set is planned, with no date.

faq.a: `provideLocale` takes an accessor, so `provideLocale(() => i18n.locale())` makes every formatter follow an i18n instance's language today, and a test covers that seam. Having i18n's own `n()` and `d()` delegate to this package is planned, not shipped.

faq.q: Does it run on iOS and Android?
faq.a: Not yet. The package is web-only. The native compiler already lowers a core set of `Intl` number and date formatting on its own; moving these functions onto it is planned, and we are not promising a date.

We have not published speed numbers for it, so this page makes no speed claim. The design is to build each `Intl` formatter once per locale and options and reuse it, in bounded tables, so formatting in a list or a binding costs one `format()` call. The size figures above are measured.

Call it directly when you format one value once. This package adds the cache, the active locale as a signal, presets, bytes and durations done right, calendar dates that do not shift, and parsing. A hand-written cache helper over `Intl` is much smaller (169 B gzip for one number, against 1.1 kB here) because it has no validation, presets, locale resolution, warnings or parsing.

faq.q: Does a date really never shift with the time zone?
faq.a: A string with no time (`2026-11-18`) or a date-time with no offset (`2026-11-18T14:30`) is a calendar value and shows that day or clock time in every zone. A string with `Z` or an offset, a number and a `Date` are instants and follow the zone. The one trap is `new Date('2026-11-18')`: that is an instant, midnight UTC.

Nullish input returns the `fallback` (an empty string by default). Invalid input returns it too, with a warning in development. A programmer error, such as an unknown unit or a malformed locale tag handed to `setLocale`, throws a `[Pyreon]` error that says how to fix it.

faq.q: Will the server and the browser print the same text?
faq.a: When both get the same locale and time zone and run the same ICU data, yes. Engines can differ in small ways (a narrow no-break space before PM), so pass the locale and zone explicitly on both sides rather than relying on each side's default.

related.name: i18n
related.text: Translations and plurals. `provideLocale(() => i18n.locale())` points every formatter at the same language.

related.name: Table
related.text: Sizes, prices and dates in cells, in the reader's format.

related.name: Zero
related.text: Request-scoped locale and time zone on the server, so concurrent requests never share one.

end.title: Say it the way they read it.
